hints: Focus on what each bar chart is really testing, solubility in ammonia for P and bond strength and exothermicity for Q.
Recall the classic ammonia test: $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{AgBr}$ needs concentrated $\text{NH}_3$, and $\text{AgI}$ stays insoluble.
Compare H-X bond strengths down the group and think how that changes how exothermic $\text{H}_2 + \text{X}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HX}$ is from Cl to I.
walkthrough:
**Check student P - solubility of AgX in ammonia**

Think about the familiar silver halide test with $\text{NH}_3(aq)$. Solubility decreases down the group.

$$\text{AgCl} \text{ (soluble in dilute } \text{NH}_3) > \text{AgBr} \text{ (soluble in conc. } \text{NH}_3) > \text{AgI} \text{ (insoluble)}$$

**Decide if P is correct**

P draws solubility increasing as $\text{Cl} < \text{Br} < \text{I}$. That is the opposite of the true trend, so P is wrong. It is a common mix up with the solubility of Group 2 hydroxides which does increase down the group.

**Check student Q - enthalpy of formation of HX**

Consider the reaction:
$$\text{H}_2(g) + \text{X}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{HX}(g)$$
All three reactions are exothermic, so $\Delta H^\circ$ is negative. As we go $\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{Br} \rightarrow \text{I}$, the H-X bond gets longer and weaker, so less energy is released.

**Decide if Q is correct**

That means the most negative $\Delta H^\circ$ is for $\text{HCl}$, then $\text{HBr}$, then $\text{HI}$ is least negative. Q shows three bars below zero with length $\text{Cl} > \text{Br} > \text{I}$, which matches perfectly, so Q is correct and only Q is correct.

options.A: Incorrect because P is wrong. P reverses the ammonia solubility trend. Only Q matches the true chemistry.
options.B: Incorrect because P alone is not right. $\text{AgI}$ is insoluble in $\text{NH}_3(aq)$ while $\text{AgCl}$ is most soluble, so P's increasing Cl to I order is backwards.
options.C: Correct. P is wrong as solubility of $\text{AgX}$ in $\text{NH}_3$ decreases Cl > Br > I. Q is right because formation of $\text{HX}$ becomes less exothermic down the group as H-X bond strength falls, giving most negative $\Delta H^\circ$ for Cl and least for I.
options.D: Incorrect because Q is correct. The $\Delta H^\circ$ bars correctly show all exothermic values with decreasing magnitude from Cl to I, so it is not true that neither is correct.
